approved: Corporations and Financial Sector Legislation Amendment Bill 2013

Said the coalition would not oppose the bill, which implements financial-sector reforms relating to over-the-counter derivatives, clearing facilities, licence reviews, regulator information sharing and reporting, while noting opposition to the government's carbon tax and support for improving the trading framework.

Argued that the bill strengthens financial-market stability by protecting clearing facilities against participant defaults, helping ASIC and the RBA focus supervision on higher-risk entities, enabling regulatory cooperation and supporting Australia's financial-services sector and G20 commitments.

The coalition will not oppose the bill, which implements G20 reforms for over-the-counter derivatives to boost transparency, reduce systemic risk, and allow ASIC and the RBA to exchange protected information with domestic and overseas regulators.
Corporations and Financial Sector Legislation Amendment Act 2013
